lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: You're listening to the Drowned Shanty Hour, from the good ship Damp Regret. The ship is fine.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The Drowned Shanty Hour. Ninety six point five five. Mind the deck. Mind the sea. Mind the other sea, under that one.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Who's listening to the Drowned Shanty Hour?

lines.speaker: The Crew
lines.text: We are, Captain!

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Good lads. So's somebody else. Look lively.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The Drowned Shanty Hour. At sea since before there was a sea. We were early. We're often early.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The Drowned Shanty Hour. Lanterns lit, fog in, and the crew in fine voice, for men this damp.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: This is the Drowned Shanty Hour. If you hear bubbles, that's applause. Thank you. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The Drowned Shanty Hour, aboard the Damp Regret. She's taken on a little water. She's taken on, in fairness, all of it.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: When we set sail, there was no sea. People forget that. We had the ship, we had the crew, we had the songs. We just didn't have anywhere to put them.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: So we sailed anyway, across nothing, singing. Water turned up about a week later. Wonderful timing. We were very pleased.

clips.title: The Wreck of the Margaret Ann

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: This next shanty is about the wreck of the Margaret Ann, which will happen in the year two thousand and ninety one. Terrible business. Lovely tune.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: If you're on the Margaret Ann, or know anyone who will be, maybe sing along. It might help. It won't. But it might.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: A word from the bridge. Some of you have written in with concerns about the ship. Let me reassure you. The ship is fine.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: She's lower in the water than she was. She's lower than the water, technically. But she's fine. Bail if you like. It's soothing.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: That was Old Pettibone on the accordion. He's sat on that barrel since the Long Calm. The squeezebox has a leak, but then, so does everything.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Nobody's asked him what's in the barrel. Nobody wants to know. It's the only dry thing on the ship.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Roll call, for the listeners. Bosun?

lines.speaker: The Crew
lines.text: Aye!

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Cook?

lines.speaker: The Crew
lines.text: Aye!

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Lookout?

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The lookout went to look out in eighteen forty, and we haven't seen him since. Which, in fairness, means he's doing it properly.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Supper tonight is the cook's sea soup. It's made of the sea. We have a great deal of sea, and the cook is nothing if not resourceful.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Seconds are available. Seconds are always available. Seconds are, in a sense, all around us.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Our cabin boy, young Tobias, turns four hundred and twelve next week. He's still the cabin boy. Promotion's slow at sea.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: I've told him. Keep your head down, sing your heart out, and in another couple of centuries you'll make deckhand.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Ahoy, the Nightjar. Relay Seven. We see your lamp up there above the fog, on the night watch, same as us. Long watches, empty seas, and a radio for company.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Different ship. Same job. This one's for you.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Morning, all. The sun's up, somewhere above us. We can see it through the water, a little wobbling coin.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Crew's on deck, stamping out the damp. Let's have a working song to get the blood going. Not that there's much of it left.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The watch reported a shadow on the water last night, with no ship above it, moving east. Small fellow. Wearing a hat. I hailed him. He said his name was Greg, and he was seeing the world.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Fair enough. That's what the sea's for. Hollis, if you're listening, he looked well. Sunburnt, for a shadow.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: When I say haul, you say away. Haul!

lines.speaker: The Crew
lines.text: Away!

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Haul!

lines.speaker: The Crew
lines.text: Away!

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Lovely. We're not hauling anything. We've nothing to haul. But it does the lungs good. Next song.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: And now the sea area forecast, issued by the Damp Regret at an hour nobody asked for.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Regret. Damp, becoming damper. Moderate, occasionally good, then poor.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Dismay. Fog. Fog later. Then more fog, from the earlier fog.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Lower Dismay. Wet. Very wet. Sea state, everywhere.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The Bottom. Calm. Quite calm. Visibility, none, but there's nothing to see.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: That's the forecast. Mind the wet.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: This is the Dog Watch, on the Drowned Shanty Hour. Short watch, long songs. All hands on deck. And under it.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Why is it called the Dog Watch? Nobody knows. We had a dog aboard once. He went over the side after a stick, in seventeen ninety.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Still swimming, I'm told. Still after the stick. You have to admire the commitment.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Evening on the Damp Regret. The lanterns are lit, the fog's come up thick, and the crew are mending the nets.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: We've no fish to catch. The nets just like being mended. Here's a slow one.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: This is Low Tide, on the Drowned Shanty Hour. The sea's gone out a little. Not far. It never goes far. It likes us.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Low Tide, and the crew are singing low. Old Pettibone's playing so soft you can hear the hull.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: She's humming along. She does that when she's happy, or when she's sinking. Hard to tell.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Three in the morning on the Damp Regret. The fog's so thick, the lantern's only a rumour.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: If you're up too, out there on a ship of your own, sing along under your breath. Shanties work best with more ghosts.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Morning, all. This is the Forenoon Watch, on the Drowned Shanty Hour. Up and singing, crew. And sweep the fish off the bunks.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Morning reports. Hull, wet. Sails, wet. Rigging, wet. Crew, wet, but cheerful. Captain, also wet, also cheerful, but in a more senior way.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Morale, high, given everything.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Breakfast is ship's biscuit. It's soft. Everything's soft. We dip it in the sea to firm it up.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Don't try that at home. Unless home is a ship. Then, honestly, you'll have worked it out.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Every year about this time, people ask if we're a ghost ship. We are not a ghost ship.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: We are a ship, with a great many ghosts on it. There's a difference, and the difference is paperwork.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: The crew have carved a turnip lantern for the bow, as is tradition. It's lit. Underwater. Don't ask me how.

lines.speaker: Captain Ezra Wetherell
lines.text: Old Pettibone says it's the most cheerful thing he's seen since the Long Calm. Then he played a very, very sad song about it.
